grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 1" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

topics.name: 1.1. TOPIC 1: NATURAL RESOURCES
topics.description: Natural resources are materials like water, air, trees, and minerals essential for life that come from nature. This topic explores the responsible use of natural resources, the relationship between population and resources, and sustainable management practices.

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC 1.1.1: NATURAL RESOURCES
sub_topics.description: Explores renewable and non-renewable natural resources, their identification, classification, and responsible utilization to prevent depletion.

competencies.description: Use renewable and non-renewable resources responsibly

sub_topics.name: 1.1.2. SUB-TOPIC 2: POPULATION AND NATURAL RESOURCES
sub_topics.description: Examines the dynamic relationship between population growth and natural resource demand, including overconsumption, environmental degradation, and sustainable management practices.

competencies.description: Analyze the relationship between population and natural resources

sub_topics.name: 1.1.3. SUB-TOPIC 3: SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCE.
sub_topics.description: Focuses on balancing human needs with environmental protection through conservation, restoration, and sustainable management practices.

competencies.description: Practise sustainable management of natural resources

topics.name: 2.1. TOPIC 2: POPULATION
topics.description: Population studies or demography scientifically investigates human populations, focusing on size, structure, distribution, and dynamics. This topic covers population composition, distribution, rapid population growth, and migration.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.1. SUB –TOPIC 1: POPULATION COMPOSITION
sub_topics.description: Covers population traits such as age, gender, density, and structure, as well as the interpretation and construction of population pyramids.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.2. SUB-TOPIC 2: POPULATION DISTRIBUTION IN ZAMBIA
sub_topics.description: Analyzes patterns, trends, and natural, social, economic, and political factors influencing population distribution across Zambia using maps and GIS tools.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.3. SUB – TOPIC 3: RAPID POPULATION GROWTH IN ZAMBIA
sub_topics.description: Examines the causes, effects, potential benefits, and actionable solutions related to rapid population growth in Zambia.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.4. SUB-TOPIC 4: MIGRATION
sub_topics.description: Investigates concepts, types, causes, and impacts of internal and international migration on places of origin and destination.

competencies.description: Apply knowledge of migration in aspects of daily life

topics.name: 1.1. TOPIC 1: SETTLEMENTS
topics.description: Settlements are fundamental aspects of human society, representing the places where people establish communities and live. They range from small villages to large metropolitan areas, reflecting diverse forms and functions across different regions and cultures. This topic will focus on identification of the various patterns of settlements, analysing factors that influence their location, identification of challenges faced by settlements and ways of resolving such challenges.

sub_topics.name: 1.1.1.SUB-TOPIC 1: SETTLEMENTS
sub_topics.description: Settlements have historically evolved from simple traditional villages to complex urban centres driven by industrialisation and globalisation. Each settlement type has its unique characteristics, challenges and opportunities, impacting both local environment and the broader region. The examination of settlements do not only provide insights on how people organise spaces and resources, but also illustrates the dynamic nature of human progress and adaptation.
learning_objectives: Identifying different types of settlements (rural and urban settlements)
Classifying settlements according to their hierarchy (homestead, hamlet, village, town, city…)
Identifying the various patterns of settlements.
Drawing the various patterns of settlements (linear/ribbon, nucleated/clustered, dispersed/Isolated).

sub_topics.name: 1.1.2. SUB TOPIC 2: LOCATION OF SETTLEMENTS
sub_topics.description: The location of settlements is one of the crucial aspect in the study of human adaptation as it influences the development, growth and sustainability of communities. Settlements have been established in various locations determined by factors such as access to water, fertility of the soils, natural resources, transportation and defence. This sub-topic is based on the factors that influence location of settlements, functions of settlements and choosing of a place to live that aligns with one’s needs and lifestyle. Understanding of these aspects is essential for appreciating the complexities of human habitation, economic development and environmental sustainability.
learning_objectives: Identifying factors that influence the location of settlements (relief, soil fertility, transport, water…).
Describing functions of different settlements (administrative, commercial, agricultural, mining…)

Choosing a place to live that aligns with one’s needs and lifestyle (considering factors such as proximity to school or work, availability of resources; water and food, transportation, options, safety and amenities…).

sub_topics.name: 1.1.3. SUB TOPIC 3: CHALLENGES IN SETTLEMENTS
sub_topics.description: Settlements, whether urban or rural, face multitude of challenges that can impact the quality of life of the residents. These challenges can be broadly categorized into environmental, social, economic, and health. The challenges can have far-reaching consequences such as decreased quality of life, increase poverty and crime, reduced economic opportunities, etc. Understanding these challenges is crucial for developing effective solutions to address them and create more sustainable, equitable, and healthy settlement.
learning_objectives: Identifying challenges faced in settlements (Rural - limited access to basic services, poor infrastructure, environmental degradation… Urban - overcrowding, inadequate infrastructure, limited access to green spaces, unemployment, environmental degradation).

Resolving challenges experienced in settlements (Rural - Sustainable agriculture, environmental conservation, clean water and sanitation campaign, health care campaigns…Urban - managing waste, urban greening, energy conservation, water conservation, sustainable urban mobility campaigns, disasters preparedness campaigns …)

topics.name: 1.2. TOPIC 2: URBANISATION
topics.description: Urbanisation is the process of people moving from rural areas to cities and urban centres, it is the global phenomenon, with increasing numbers of people living in urban areas. Zambia’s urban population is growing rapidly with significant implications for economies, societies, and environments. The country has experienced significant urbanisation in recent decades, driven by physical, social and economic factors. Major cities like Lusaka, Kitwe, and Ndola are hubs of economic activities, innovation, and cultural diversity. Urbanisation in Zambia presents both opportunities for economic growth and development, as well as challenges such as housing shortages, infrastructure strain, and environmental degradation. Understanding urbanisation in Zambia is crucial for addressing the country’s development challenges and promoting sustainable urban growth. This topic will explore the relationship between urbanisation, daily lives and the environment

competencies.description: Relate urbanisation to daily lives and environment.

sub_topics.name: 1.2.1. SUB- TOPIC 1: URBANISATION
sub_topics.description: Urbanisation happens worldwide, and many people now live in urban areas. Urbanisation brings good things like economic growth but also problems like not enough houses, crowded roads, and harm to the environment. To help Zambia grow in a smart and sustainable way, we need to understand how urbanisation affects daily life and nature.
learning_objectives: Discussing causes of rapid urbanisation (physical, social and economic factors)
Analysing the impacts of urbanisation in different areas (Business owners, farmers and town planners…)

Relating urbanisation to daily lives and the environment (Basic Problem solving, learning different cultures and life styles, road safety and traffic congestion solutions, clean-up and tree planting, appreciating local community growth … )

competencies.description: Relate urbanisation to daily lives and environment.
